# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document accompanies
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md) and
> expands the RFC's phase sequence into **independently committable and independently verifiable**
> three-level tasks.
>
> The phase sequence and acceptance gates are governed exclusively by the body of RFC-039; this
> document is responsible only for decomposing the work into executable granularity and registering
> conflicts that remain undecided.

## Positioning and Scope

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                               |
| ----------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, corresponding one-to-one to RFC-039's phase sequence                                          |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, each of which can be staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 268         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                           |

**Unused numbers are not recycled**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP
route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unused (2026-11-25). None of these three
has had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established—the full history of this document has
zero matches for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1` (verifiable via
`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md`), and there are no
repository-wide references. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test revival and
completion): that phase has been split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8's numbering aligns
with its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so on).

**Covered here**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding acceptance
criteria.

**Not covered here**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the justification for phase
ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered level-2/level-3 rows **must
contain two fields**—**Owning Phase** (the P to which the task truly belongs, which may differ from
its chapter) and **Blocks Mainline**; `registration pending scheduling` is no longer the default
state, and an unmarked item is considered **not schedulable**. Numbers **must be unique across the
entire document** (tasks in external tracks use the track number, such as `029g.x`, and must not
occupy `N.x`).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: checked rows contain only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number, if any—written on one
line: `- [x] **3.24.1 remaining pattern-matching work** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not write
the fix, a criterion chain, gate thresholds, file line numbers, test names, or review conclusions**:
those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a kanban board, not a
process chronicle. **Do not write decision labels or restate conclusions**: “user decision A/B/C,”
“option A,” “the final implementation is…” and similar wording do not belong here—the board answers
only whether something is complete; decisions and results are recorded in commit messages and the
RFC-039 decision register.

**Short hashes are authoritative only after pushing**: closure rows contain the short hash on
`origin/dev` after the push. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then write the
closure row** (see [commit-convention](../commit-convention.md), “Commit numbers are taken after
push”). The closure commit itself does not carry a hash—self-reference is impossible.

**The count column contains only numbers**: the level-1/2/3 counts under `Positioning and Scope`
contain only the current values; increment/decrement history such as `+1 = …` does not belong in the
table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “implementation points” from eight documents into the main table, **five
hard gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been closed:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Resolution                                                                                                                                   |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC-039 defines P5 (checker splitting) and acceptance criterion C1 zero-diff, but none of the seven documents describes how to perform the split; `01-routing.md` contains one mention of `annotations.rs` in its directory tree, the only mention in the entire batch                                                                                   | P5's steps are supplied here (see below)                                                                                                     |
| G2  | **The three ownership assignments for the `include!` refactor resulted in zero implementation**. RFC-039 lists it under P4; `02` assigns the reference to itself; `06` S7 also lists it. However, `02`'s change list (6 additions + 20 modifications) does **not include `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                         | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 here (prerequisite: P4 complete); references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here             |
| G3  | **Three coexisting lists of CI scripts**. `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py`; `01` lists four scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` lists four different checks; `04` also previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | The unified list appears in §P9 of this document (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to this table       |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life cycle of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1005 lines that need revival,” while B6 in the same document says it “must be deleted together with” the `Precedence` enum; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                               | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision record C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted)                                                        |
| G5  | **Conflict in the wording of the L2 objective**: RFC-039 and this directory's index previously stated “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | It has converged on a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Reason for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (no fabrication / no endless filling / no patching
when a refactor is required) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established before
work begins; otherwise, when P1 revives tests, it will already be adding `mod` declarations to
`tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Vulnerabilities (Minimal Solution)

Source: [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3, vulnerability-fix half + **2026-10-07
silent-drop-point audit (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, decision of 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect for which “the old behavior does not count as success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack overflow, silently
> incorrect answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactor**, but all four requirements must be
> met: ① red before green (the red criterion must exist first and genuinely be red); ② the
> externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled successfully and ran
> correctly” must not change (they must not become failures, and their existing diagnostic codes /
> text / exit codes must not be removed or changed); ③ register it in the same commit (mark the
> error type on this row + add a revision note for the phase + include the “Error Type” line in the
> PR's required block); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff.
> **Category D user-visible semantics / E external-contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must
> still receive a decision first. See
> [07 §Routing Criteria for Semantic Corrections](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the expanded
> criteria and the A–F whitelist; the “default super-refactor + post-hoc registration” approach is
> not adopted** (rationale: RFC-039 D59: a zero-red criterion cannot distinguish a fix from a
> regression, and conflicts with “C5′ does not exist” and “no relaxation of any kind”).

**Acceptance**: vulnerability criteria turn green, and **deliberately removing the fix must turn
them red again**. **Risk**: adding E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have red criteria first (changing code first is prohibited);
3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 use C2/C3 and the 9.2 gate in P9. **Risk**: the new W1002
diagnostic is a behavior change, and the corpus differential baseline and CHANGELOG must be updated
in sync.

> **Fast-stop lane**: P3 need not wait for all of P2. The sole hard prerequisites for 3.1/3.2 are
> **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two red criteria)**; 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (IR
> verifier, snapshots, single-file differential, performance baseline) can proceed in parallel with
> P3. Stopping the bleeding from a correctness vulnerability (`Sorted(3)` silently passing) must not
> be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure construction. 3.3 (panic-to-diagnostic conversion) has no
> prerequisites and can land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint**, and is distinct from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (narrowing
Rust visibility to `pub(crate)`).

**Why the whole track must precede P4**: 029g's deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of
all four refactoring phases; reversing the order would require repeating the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new SSA IR.

| 029g deletion surface                                               | File                                                                                                               | Rewritten by which phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KwPub` and grammar branches                                        | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexical convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 split `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory renaming (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                         |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the pub branch of `collect_exports`         | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (the `include!`→true `mod` conversion and checker split are **pure moves**, and the pub branch will be moved unchanged into the new files)                                                                                                          |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (`check_project` slimming)                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `semantic_tokens`' `Public` modifier                                | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `ir_gen`'s `is_pub`-ignoring binding                                | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (`ir_gen.rs` SSA conversion)                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| 31 occurrences of `pub` in `src/std/`                               | `std/list.yx` / `json.yx` / `option.yx` / `result.yx`                                                              | No phase directly changes them, but **P6's hard acceptance requires zero differences in `src/std/` (`git diff --stat src/std/` is empty; directly driven tests under `tests/` are exempt, see P6's hard-acceptance section)**—they can only land before P6 |

**Additional benefit**: 029g deletes the dead `env.exports` table (populated in production but never
consumed anywhere) and the `is_exported`/`is_visible` accessors ⇒ P4's 4.3 obligation ledger loses
one “produced but never consumed” field.

**Acceptance (behavior changes; red criterion first)**:

1. **Red before green**: each of the two behavior changes must first land a red criterion before
   code is changed—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ② unreferenced
   top-level bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (previously pub items were absolutely
   exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` test case from
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, equivalent new cases must replace
   them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff requires an
   explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` all pass.

**Ordering**: it overlaps 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`)⇒ the two must be serial and
cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; implementers decide which to start based on available context.

> **Commit comparison (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (the P3.5 chapter + the
> main-chain/constraint row) was merged into `97071c81b` together with RFC-039's D56 during a
> parallel-flow cleanup of the workspace; that commit's message records “3.4 addendum registration +
> D57/D58 decisions recorded” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten, and it is
> registered in place under the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing
> note) as evidence for later bisection.

This changes the shape of `overload_resolutions` keys and mixed IR names, and is D59 **Category D** (requires a decision). **Disposition in this round (after the two narrowing rounds of 4.9.9)**: 4.9.9 **introduces no new rejection**—the prior six rounds' Category D rejection lists (all named arguments always E1014 / conflicting positional-argument forms always E1107 / E5006 ambiguity prohibition at import-name resolution) are deleted and all are void; **Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is ever migrated with the annotation family, **then** `checker.rs` must add a
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that this import remains unchanged; 5.3 **did not
migrate** it according to measurement, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Split only confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules that are only 200–400 lines—that
increases navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields no decoupling benefit. The remaining
submodules (signatures / type_defs / imports) are deferred until their files grow back to 1,500
lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62's end state is a **unified term world**—type positions and value positions share
> the same set of compile-time terms. One strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site actual view and the
> implementation-header binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is **pure
> determination** (the two sides are identical after normalization; no type variables are bound);
> evidence is the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals / value environment /
> single-value pinning / Γ equalities); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (holding for
> closed terms as well as open terms / recursion); Σ construction points **reuse** the same evidence
> interface and do not establish a separate one. **Completion criterion = the invariants hold, not
> that all subphase names are checked off.**

> **A.C3 prerequisite: F4 decision (decided as A on 2026-11-16, with measurement)**: the old wording
> “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter requests” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly` have been
> deleted; the current mechanism is that open-term `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒ no request is
> created, and the representation `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can hold `k-1`. **The decision was
> changed to two orthogonal decisions + one termination subdecision**: D-a representation (A: open
> terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before enqueueing / B: no specialization); D-b
> evaluation point (only mono is allowed; C-1: reconstructing the second field and C-2: restoring it
> from IR both break the single representation / evaluator, so C-3 = A); **F4-T termination** (naive
> firing causes the recursive chain to hit `max_depth` and trigger E3005; T-a: instantiate the
> condition inside the term / T-b: bounded firing + fallback to the original at the boundary / T-c:
> a termination layer or a change to the specification). **Do [the measurement] first, then decide;
> before measurement, “A is implementable” must not be treated as a conclusion.** **User
> (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task and
> does not claim the complete I4 form.**

> **B.d prerequisite: determination-point protocol (not yet written)**: RFC-027 §12.1 specifies that
> “determination points use unification first; after unification fails, definitional equality may be
> attempted, but the partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled
> back.” The implementation must answer: whether the entry point is an outer wrapper around
> `solver.unify` or a new `decide` layer; whether defeq is attempted only when both sides are ground
> (no unbound variables); the snapshot / restoration boundary and cost; and whether unify and defeq
> share one budget or each has its own. **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for
> subtyping / Any / Never; defeq determines equivalence only and does not take over subtyping;
> bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol
> and production call graph before writing code**; the wiring contract for 6.9.3c was wasted for two
> rounds by assuming that `can_assign` was the determination point, while `AssignmentChecker` has
> zero production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero corpus /
> IR-snapshot drift or item-by-item classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected integration
> tests; ③ error-code generator idempotence (if an emission point / code table changed); ④ behavior
> changes classified under D59 and implemented red before green. **Wiring tasks additionally
> require**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how many paths, which
> path is reachable); using unit-test reachability as a substitute for user reachability is
> prohibited; rollback and budget must have measured numbers. **Residual disposition**: #537
> (Category D, proof-function formal refinement is silently dropped; do not fix before the decision,
> and 6.9.4 / 6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0; Category C boundary; if
> it is not closed, 6.9.4 covers only module-internal forms), #540 (deep-nesting stack overflow;
> **closed**—3.20.30 closed on 2026-11-14: orchestrator-layer 64MB large-stack thread + parser depth
> gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019; see row 3.20.30 in 09), #541 (TailCall; **closed**—three
> synchronized changes on 2026-11-16: `call_form_is_rewritten` / `replace_calls_in_function` /
> `drop_erased_call_args` cover `Call`/`TailCall` through the single rewritten-call-target site; the
> init section and function bodies share one site-rewriting implementation; red→green + three
> mutations), #542 (isolated shared layer; **implemented (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono
> two-entry wiring + C2c temporary workaround removal; red→green, 402/402, function-table
> attribution and deviations), #552 (imported multi-parameter predicate proof execution; adjacent to
> 6.9.5, assigned separately). **Ownership pending a decision**: the four open-constraint tripwires
> in `rfc027_refined_transparency` (`Eq(N, n)`) do not belong to 6.9.4's constant-equality bridge;
> leave them within 6.9.4's outOfScope or move them to 6.9.1 / the E4018 proof-function surface; a
> decision is required.

> **Non-claims / boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch
> Π/`DepFn`, and does not claim the complete Π/Σ form; 6.9.4 covers only constant equalities and

**Hard acceptance** (**revised on 2026-10-27, following decision ② of 2026-10-26**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round from 6.1
through 6.7**. **Directly driven test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive changed
code, such as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) **may** be modified when mechanical changes require
it, but each change must register the **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be deleted
and assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral fix** batch (new
diagnostic codes + baseline update), does not follow this hard acceptance rule, and is handled as a
separate round with a separate decision.

> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, treating all of `tests/` as requiring zero differences; the
> current wording **changes only directly driven test files from “zero differences” to “may be
> changed but must register file / line count / reason”**; the **zero-difference requirement remains
> unchanged for the corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer (`tests/baselines`), and

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority, and missing a consumer silently changes
associativity (no error, only a different parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and operator-property cross-validation tests; every new operator must enter both the
table and the cross-validation test.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on D0/D2 from `08`**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or action
> code refers back to `sema`, it will be blocked by `check-boundary.py`.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 fast-stop lane (decision of 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed to **2.3.2 +
> 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR verifier, 2.2
> snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential and performance baseline) can proceed in parallel with P3.
> Stopping the bleeding from a correctness vulnerability must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x adds `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must be **written red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3), and the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order would fossilize bugs as “established behavior” in the phase table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)'s deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list appears in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated, otherwise regressions cannot be located by bisection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If the type representation does not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; **the P7 gate = exits A/B/C of 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; that is, 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and 6.9.4 complete), while D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume the quantifier-derived views and defeq interface, but must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a prerequisite for P7, is not subject to this gate, and must not consume the undecided defeq / quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The final form of 9.5's snapshot baseline and 9.3's `pub(crate)` leak count is taken only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

### Parallelizable Groups

| Group                                    | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **A (the only group authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                                |
| B                                        | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| C                                        | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| D                                        | 4.4 (proof-layer completion) ∥ the entire P6 line                                  | `02` explicitly says in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1–S4”                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| E                                        | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All are mutually independent after 4.1                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| F                                        | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced by P0 can be developed in parallel) | 9.5's snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| G                                        | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` declarations under `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pair overlaps) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (the same
batch file for B6/E5); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (now unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track's pub-deletion batch and the silent-channel
fix must be serial).

**New internal documentation constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the pure-move batch preceding P7), and 7b's `Phi` arm must
precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is a separate phase rather than part of P9**—gates are “after-the-fact checks,” whereas rules
  are “before-the-fact judgment.” P9's scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor was
  required”; only D0–D4's review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the three coexisting lists in original gap G3
  made closure impossible. This table merges them into 10 active scripts, each owned by one phase
  (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and hard-transition points
  explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to implement after
  the refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039
  D56). Deferring it until after the refactor means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar,
  new checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and
  RFC status correction into S4.
- **P5's steps are supplemented here rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the granularity at which work can be
  rolled back.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero call-site changes” as hard acceptance**—the split must be independently
  revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixes for exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it says only that “fixed defects
  must not be rolled back” and lacks a requirement to record what was fixed. **Execution
  convention**: the commit message for every 1.3.x fix must reference the fixed test name and the
  defect description as evidence for later bisection.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two
  exclusive commits per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 references must be renamed; missing one
  **silently changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as 7e.1,
  and D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34's opcode reclamation was merged into 7e.1, and the deletion
  action landed in P10 S6.1 (6753bbe).
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned an “independent issue”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: `2341` was incorporated as 7e.3; `2315` was rechecked on 2026-11-28 and
  found to be an audit false positive (the field has no producer, and the language layer has no
  throw/try/catch); 7e.2 was cancelled, and the residual exception machinery was deleted by P10 S6.1
  (6753bbe).
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into the
  generation-time gate task in P10 S6.2 and implemented (a2e570c).

> converged into the [RFC-039 decision register](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md)
> (D1–D50).** No pending items remain here. Item-by-item mapping:

| Original number | Issue                                                                          | Decision                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1              | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8                      | **Revive** (the prerequisite for P1 is that revival involves tests with genuine assertions); P8 no longer deletes the file (Pratt is retained)                                  |
| C2              | “Grammar-driven” promise vs table-driven implementation                        | **Fallback solution**: retain Pratt + a single declarative precedence table + cross-validation of two `BinOp` sets from one source (the LALRPOP route is withdrawn); see P8 8.3 |
| C3              | C6 category definition conflicts with S1 classification                        | **S1 belongs to C6** (revival does not require an equivalence criterion, only regression tests); C6's definition is expanded to “pure deletion or pure revival”                 |
| C4              | `test_release_plan_spans_consumed` whitelist                                   | **No whitelist**; the difference set must be empty; if that is impossible, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change to `PlanId` (D20/D41)                               |
| C5              | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions were not verified | **P4's 4.2.7 explicitly lists verification as mandatory**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                                                   |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4's `ProgramKind`                            | **The wasm-path defect fix is merged into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                                                |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                             | **Assigned to 04** (P7 batch c), see D21                                                                                                                                        |
| C8              | `upvalue_count` correction and the `.42` version number                        | **Fix + change `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14–16`), see D17                                         |
